items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: Lawrence Toka and I went to work with Alphonse Picou at the Rialto nightclub... Who else was in the band? Lawrence Picou, Johnny David, Ernest Milton and myself.

ctx.x: I played in Mobile, with Slim Hunter, broadcast at Battle House in Mobile, at that radio station there, broadcast. Battle House there, with Slim Hunter out there, that's right. That was in Mobile. What did Slim play? Banjo. He was a great entertainer, great songs and a banjo. Well, what was the first band you played with when you came over here? The first band I came here when I played with? When I first landed in New Orleans, I mean, coming to stay to work, because the Afroans people…
Ernest Milton played what? Drummer. And Johnny Dave played what?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And one of the Dave, like Johnny Dave, banjo. Oh, yeah.

ctx.x: George Stewart. What did he play?

Clarinet? Sax. Sax. Most of the clarinet in that time, but he played a little sax too also. That George Stewart. I don't know if he's still living yet. I don't know. And one of the Dave, like Johnny Dave, banjo. Oh, yeah.
